name: Alkoclar height treatment

lead: Alkoclar is the name used on height forums for a patented formulation and programme linked to Erdal Can Alkoclar, a Turkish inventor. It is described as a growth-supporting formula for children and young adults, and forum posters repeat claims that it can add several centimetres of height within a year.

The topic is discussed mainly on looksmax.org. Posts cite a patent describing a somatotropic composition and quote statements attributed to Alkoclar about results and side effects, but no peer-reviewed trial results are cited in those threads.

paras: According to forum posters, the formula is obtained directly from Alkoclar as a year-long supply, taken alongside a routine, with growth said to depend on age and open growth plates. These accounts are second-hand and the product details are not independently documented here.

One forum poster quotes a statement attributed to the inventor that earlier chronic-use versions caused side effects, including carpal-tunnel-like symptoms and prostate effects in some participants. Forum members also raise concerns about the cost, long timeline and refund terms. No regulator approval is cited.

angle.text: Proponents say the formula can increase height in younger people, with figures like 5 to 8 cm mentioned in forums. These figures are reported by posters and not backed by published trial data in the cited threads.

lead: The Alkoclar height treatment refers, in looksmaxxing and height-increase forums, to a formulation and programme associated with Erdal Can Alkoclar, a Turkish scientist and entrepreneur. Forum posts describe him as holder of many patents, including one for a somatotropic composition intended for dwarfism and late-growth conditions.[1][2]

People interested in height discuss it as a possible way for adolescents and young adults to gain several centimetres, with one thread poster repeating a story of a young man growing almost 8 cm in under a year.[2] Another thread describes the claimed routine as adding 5 to 8 cm.[3]

The claims come from forum discussion and statements attributed to the inventor. Posts say he announced closing a study without publishing all the data, and describe side effects in earlier versions of the formula.[1] No clinical studies are cited in the threads.
infobox: About 7,000 euros for a year's supply (forum reports)

paras: A forum poster describes Alkoclar as a Turkish scientist and millionaire who claimed some years ago to have discovered a compound that makes people grow, originally framed as a medicine for achondroplasia.[1] A quoted statement attributed to him says his former R&D team patented more than 154 methylprotodioscin derivatives with uses ranging from neurogenesis and myogenesis to height increase, while noting inconsistent results from the oral formulation.[1]
One thread describes a patent as a somatotropic composition that helps dwarfism and late growth syndromes and increases expression of a growth-related mRNA.[2]

Forum users report that the formula is offered as a year's supply at about 7,000 euros with a money-back guarantee, and that free trials have been promised for years but not delivered; these are individual accounts.[3][2] One poster, aged 18, wrote that he planned to try it and described earlier use of other height approaches such as hormone products.[2]
Other members questioned the reliability of the claims, arguing that a large pharmaceutical company would have bought a formula that worked.[2]

In one thread a poster states that 4 of 7 participants in an earlier study experienced severe carpal-tunnel-like symptoms with loss of limb function and that participants also had prostate inflammation and raised PSA levels.[1] These statements are second-hand forum quotations.

lore.intro: The formula is discussed on looksmax.org as a possible alternative to growth-hormone-based height approaches, with debate over its legitimacy and price.[3][2]
